selectedScope: What is the DNA double helix?
sources.paraphrase: DNA has sugar/phosphate chains and internal complementary A–T and C–G pairs. The two strands have opposite directions. Humans also carry a mitochondrial genome. Nuclear DNA is packaged as chromosomes.
sources.limits: No claims derived from its simplified eye-colour example, universal inheritance wording, gene percentages or condensed-chromosome framing. No source image copied.

selectedScope: failure to detect higher-order fibers in studied human SAEC nuclei and induced chicken-nucleus comparator
discussion contrasting observed human packing and induced fibers
conclusion that discrete higher-order fibers are not necessary for compaction
sources.paraphrase: In the studied human cell systems, chromatin was irregularly packed rather than an obligatory set of higher-order fibers. The authors detected induced fibers in a separate treated chicken-nucleus preparation. This bounds the drawing: irregular packing is illustrative, and a universal 30-nm ladder is unwarranted.
supports: no mandatory hierarchy or universal 30-nm fiber
sources.limits: Selected primary text only; no full Methods/supplement, source-image inspection, raw-data reanalysis or universal absence-of-fibers claim. No empirical diameters, concentrations or quantitative chromosome packing in the artwork.
